properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures of 36 degrees or lower will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Oregon and southwest
Washington.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a 20-30% chance that temperatures
will fall below 32 degrees, especially for locations that do not
develop fog. Frost and freeze headlines are only issued through the
growing season of April 1 through October 31. Therefore, frost or
freeze headlines will not be issued beginning November 1, even
though similar low temperatures are possible. Frost and freeze
headlines will no longer be issued this growing season for the
Upper Hood River Valley, southern Willamette Valley, south
Washington Cascade Foothills, and north Oregon Coast Range as these
locations have already experienced a hard freeze earlier in
October.
properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 30 at 10:13PM PDT until October 31 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants.

NWSheadline: FROST ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM PDT SATURDAY

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Martin County in east central Florida...
Southeastern St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 352 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2.5 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Walton, Stuart, Indiantown, Jupiter Island, Palm City, Port
Salerno, Jensen Beach, Hobe Sound, Sewall's Point, Witham Field,
North River Shores, Hobe Sound Beach, Nettles Island, Jonathan
Dickinson State Park, Ocean Breeze Park, Rio, Hobe Sound Wildlife
Refuge, Waveland and Hutchinson Island South.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San Pablo
Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31 and 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
counties, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin, and Brevard.

* WHEN...From 10 AM EST this morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Some
roads may flood. Minor tidal flooding along the coast may be
exacerbated by heavy rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An approaching disturbance from the Gulf is forecast to interact
with unusually rich moisture over portions of Central Florida,
causing bands of heavy rain today through Monday afternoon. The
ground is nearly saturated, especially along the Treasure Coast
urban corridor. Widespread amounts of 1-3 inches are forecast,
with localized amounts of 5 inches or more which may cause flash
flooding.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from late Sunday night
through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves
can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people
into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on Sunday
11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 31 at 5:58PM PDT until November 3 at 8:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory,
until 7 PM EST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 1:39AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31, and 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are expected over

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 31 at 9:36PM EDT until November 1 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the

signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following
areas, Hualapai Mountains, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead -
AZ side, Lake Mohave - AZ side, Northwest Deserts and Northwest
Plateau, southeast California, including the following area, San
Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley, and Nevada,
including the following areas, Lake Mead - NV side, Lake Mohave -
NV side, Lincoln County and Northeast Clark County.

* WHEN...Now through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moderate to heavy rain is possible at times. Between a half an
inch and an inch of rain will be possible. With saturated soils
and significant run off expected, flash flooding  may occur.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 12:31AM PDT until November 1 at 2:30AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 7000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to 10 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of up to 3 inches possible down to 6000
feet.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 7000 feet, including Highway 50 and
Interstate 80.

* WHEN...From 8 AM PDT Saturday to 7 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels initially 7000 to 8000 feet
Saturday, lowering to 6000 to 7000 feet Saturday night into Sunday.
Heaviest snowfall expected Saturday evening into Sunday. Light
flurries possible down to 5000 feet on Saturday night into Sunday,
but no accumulations expected below 6000 feet.
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 2:19PM PDT until November 1 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.instruction:

quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 1 at 2:57PM EST until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

forecast.

forecast.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with

submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Friday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures of 36 degrees or lower will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...In Oregon, Clackamas County Cascade Foothills, East Central
Willamette Valley, Tualatin Valley, West Central Willamette Valley,
and Central Oregon Coast Range Lowlands. In Washington, North Clark
County Lowlands.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 9 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a 20-30% chance that temperatures
will fall below 32 degrees, especially for locations that do not
develop fog. Frost and freeze headlines are only issued through the
growing season of April 1 through October 31. Therefore, frost or
freeze headlines will not be issued beginning November 1, even
though similar low temperatures are possible. Frost and freeze
headlines will no longer be issued this growing season for the
Upper Hood River Valley, southern Willamette Valley, south
Washington Cascade Foothills, and north Oregon Coast Range as these
locations have already experienced a hard freeze earlier in
October.
properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 30 at 10:23AM PDT until October 31 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help

properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures of 36 degrees or lower will result in frost
formation.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Oregon and southwest
Washington.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 9 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a 20-30% chance that temperatures
will fall below 32 degrees, especially for locations that do not
develop fog. Frost and freeze headlines are only issued through the
growing season of April 1 through October 31. Therefore, frost or
freeze headlines will not be issued beginning November 1, even
though similar low temperatures are possible. Frost and freeze
headlines will no longer be issued this growing season for the
Upper Hood River Valley, southern Willamette Valley, south
Washington Cascade Foothills, and north Oregon Coast Range as these
locations have already experienced a hard freeze earlier in
October.
properties.headline: Frost Advisory issued October 30 at 10:23AM PDT until October 31 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender outdoor plants from the cold.
Consider temporarily moving outdoor potted plants indoors if they are
sensitive to cold temperatures.

Consider temporarily covering sensitive plants with a lightweight
cotton fabric (i.e., bedsheets, thin blankets), as this will help
retain heat and provide frost protection for your plants.

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Okeechobee County in east central Florida...

producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 5 and 9 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are

flash flooding.

urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Whispering Pines, Okeechobee Airport and Basswood Estates.

the City of Okeechobee are impassable. Motorists should avoid these
roads. Water was also entering structures.

properties.description:

High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 7 feet
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal portions of Saint Lucie and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday night. For
the High Surf Advisory, from 5 PM this afternoon to 7 PM EST
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 31 at 1:38AM EDT until November 1 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent east-northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the
St John River have slowed flow at Astor. Forecast rainfall may lead
to additional rises within Moderate flood stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.4 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
An upper-level low will move atop Florida today through Monday. This
feature will add more moisture and support for showers and storms
than recent days. Strong low-level easterly flow will result in bands
of repeated rainfall for isolated to scattered locations. Showers and
storms are expected to be a bit more widespread with higher rain
rates than the past few days.

* WHAT...Bands of heavy rain may cause urban and street flooding.

* WHERE...All of Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties.

* WHEN...From 10 AM EST this morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered area of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Uncertainty is high regarding exactly where the highest rain
amounts will fall. However, scattered locations across the east
coast may pick up 3 to 5 inches of rain through Monday. Isolated
spots may see accumulations as high as 5 to 7 inches. These
amounts may fall over a window of a few hours. Expected impacts
could be greater than forecast if the heaviest rainfall occurs
near the coast during times of high tide.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Miami-Dade, FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Miami-Dade County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1107 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Black Point, Goulds, Cutler Bay, West Perrine, Princeton, Zoo
Miami, Richmond Heights, South Miami Heights and Palmetto
Estates.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Highlands
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Florida, including the following
county, Highlands.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An approaching disturbance from the Gulf is forecast to interact
with unusually high moisture over portions of Central Florida,
causing bands of heavy rain today through Monday afternoon. The
ground is nearly saturated, especially over Highlands County.
Widespread amounts of 1-3 inches are forecast, with localized
amounts of 5 inches or more which may cause flash flooding.
- Highlands County
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
